title: Bolivian National Revolution of April 1952
note: April 9 date, MNR, street fighting in La Paz, Paz Estenssoro returning from exile in Argentina — all confirmed.

title: Universal Suffrage Extended to Bolivia's Indigenous Majority
note: Electorate expanded from ~200,000 to over 1 million confirmed. Decree issued June 24 / July 21 1952.

title: Tin Mines Nationalized; COMIBOL Created
note: COMIBOL created October 2, nationalization of Patino/Hochschild/Aramayo on October 31 confirmed.

title: Agrarian Reform Decree Redistributes Land to Indigenous Peasants
note: Decree signed August 2, 1953 at Ucureña; pongueaje abolition confirmed.

title: US Extends Diplomatic Recognition and Economic Aid to MNR
note: US recognition and food aid to prevent further radicalization confirmed by primary source.

title: Petroleum Code Opens Oil Sector to Foreign Investment
note: 1955 petroleum code inviting foreign investment into eastern lowlands confirmed by Britannica.

title: IMF Stabilization Plan Curbs Hyperinflation
note: 1956 IMF stabilization plan confirmed; ended the post-revolutionary inflationary spiral.

title: Alliance for Progress Channels Major Development Aid to Bolivia
note: Alliance for Progress was launched by Kennedy in 1961, not 1960. Year is off by 1+.

title: Bolivia Breaks Diplomatic Relations with Chile Over Lauca River
note: Diplomatic break April 17, 1962 confirmed; Chile diverted Lauca unilaterally.

title: Military Coup Ends Twelve Years of MNR Rule
note: Coup November 3–4, 1964; Barrientos and Ovando confirmed. MNR governed April 1952–November 1964 (12 years).

title: Barrientos Junta Violently Suppresses Mining Unions
note: Military occupation of mine camps and dissolution of union leadership under Barrientos confirmed.

title: Che Guevara Captured and Executed in Bolivia
note: Captured October 8, executed October 9, 1967 near La Higuera. CIA-trained Bolivian forces confirmed.

title: San Juan Massacre of Miners at Catavi-Siglo XX
note: June 24, 1967 confirmed; ~20 killed and 70 wounded at Catavi-Siglo XX during midsummer night celebrations.

title: General Ovando Nationalizes Gulf Oil Assets
note: Coup September 26; Gulf Oil nationalization decree October 17, 1969 confirmed.

title: Hugo Banzer Right-Wing Coup Overthrows Torres Government
note: August 21, 1971 confirmed; Brazilian support confirmed; Torres overthrown confirmed.

title: Bolivia Begins Natural Gas Pipeline Exports to Argentina
note: Bolivia-Argentina gas export agreement and pipeline confirmed; major foreign exchange source.

title: Cochabamba Valley Massacre of Peasants at Tolata-Epizana
note: January 1974 confirmed; peasants blockaded roads protesting food prices; army fired on them. Death toll disputed (80–200) but event facts match.

title: Charana Summit Attempts Bolivia-Chile Sea Access Breakthrough
note: February 8, 1975 summit confirmed; failed due to Peru's veto rights, not internal Chilean opposition as stated — minor framing discrepancy, core facts correct.

title: Bolivia Joins Operation Condor Transnational Repression Network
note: Bolivia's participation in Operation Condor confirmed; US-backed network targeting exiles confirmed.

title: Miners' Wives Hunger Strike Challenges Banzer Dictatorship
note: Event year is wrong: the hunger strike began December 28, 1977 (not 1976). Year off by 1+.

title: Fraudulent Election and Collapse of Banzer Regime
note: 1978 election fraud, annulment, Pereda coup against Banzer, and chaotic succession confirmed.

title: Garcia Meza Cocaine Coup Installs Narco-Military State
note: July 17, 1980 confirmed; narco-trafficker funding confirmed; Klaus Barbie paramilitary role confirmed.

title: Democratic Restoration: Siles Zuazo Ends Military Rule
note: Siles Zuazo took office October 10, 1982 confirmed; ended Garcia Meza military era.

title: Severe El Nino Drought Devastates Altiplano Agriculture
note: 1982–83 El Niño drought severely hit Bolivian Altiplano agriculture, confirmed by UN relief reports.

title: Hyperinflation Accelerates Beyond 20,000 Percent
note: Inflation exceeded 20,000% confirmed; some sources cite peak at ~26,000% annualized in 1985, so 20,000% by mid-1985 is accurate.

title: Shock Therapy Decree 21060 Ends Hyperinflation
note: August 29, 1985 confirmed; inflation dropped to near zero within months confirmed.

title: International Tin Council Collapse Triggers Mass COMIBOL Layoffs
note: ITC collapse October 1985 confirmed; tin price halved confirmed. Layoff figure stated as 20,000+ — sources cite 25,000–30,000; minor discrepancy, directionally correct.

title: Miners' March to La Paz Crushed Under State of Siege
note: 1986 miners' march from Oruro toward La Paz, state of siege, and COB leader arrests confirmed.

title: Operation Blast Furnace: US Military Enters Bolivia for Drug War
note: July 1986, US Army Rangers and DEA with 6 Black Hawks confirmed; Chapare/Beni operations confirmed.

title: Displaced Miners Flood Chapare; Coca Economy Expands
note: Post-1985 miner migration to Chapare and coca expansion confirmed; Evo Morales connection confirmed.

title: Law 1008 Criminalizes Chapare Coca Production Under US Pressure
note: Law 1008 enacted 1988 under US pressure, Yungas vs Chapare distinction confirmed.

title: Indigenous March for Territory and Dignity Reshapes Politics
note: 34-day march from Trinidad to La Paz confirmed; arrived La Paz September 19, 1990.

title: Victor Hugo Cardenas Becomes First Indigenous Vice President
note: First Aymara vice president, 1993 election with Sanchez de Lozada confirmed.

title: Law of Popular Participation Creates 311 New Municipalities
note: 1994 decentralization law creating new municipalities confirmed.

title: Capitalization Reform Privatizes State Enterprises
note: 1994 capitalization of YPFB, ENTEL, Lloyd Aereo Boliviano confirmed under Sanchez de Lozada.

title: Bolivia-Brazil Gas Pipeline Agreement Signed
note: Agreement signed 1995, pipeline (Gasbol) inaugurated 1999. Description says 1998 — minor discrepancy (actual inauguration 1999), but agreement year 1995 is correct.

title: Evo Morales Elected Head of Chapare Coca Growers Federation
note: Morales elected executive secretary of the Six Federations of Cochabamba Tropics mid-1990s confirmed.

title: Plan Dignidad: Militarized Forced Coca Eradication Launched
note: Plan Dignidad launched under Banzer 1997, US-funded forced eradication in Chapare confirmed.

title: Cochabamba Water War Forces Reversal of Privatization
note: April 2000 confirmed; Victor Hugo Daza (17-year-old) killed confirmed; Aguas del Tunari expelled confirmed.

title: Peasant Roadblocks Paralyze Bolivia for Weeks
note: September-October 2000 peasant roadblocks confirmed; deaths in security force clashes confirmed.

title: Gas War: 60 Killed; Sanchez de Lozada Flees Bolivia
note: ~60 killed confirmed (prosecutor cited 64); El Alto confirmed; Sanchez de Lozada fled October 17-18, 2003 confirmed.

title: National Gas Referendum Mandates State Control of Hydrocarbons
note: July 2004 referendum with 90%+ supporting state gas ownership confirmed.

title: Evo Morales Wins Presidency with Historic 53.7% Majority
note: 53.7% result confirmed; first outright majority since return of democracy confirmed.

title: Morales Issues Decree 28701 Nationalizing Hydrocarbons on May Day
note: May 1, 2006, Decree 28701, 56 installations occupied, 82% revenue share for large fields — all confirmed.

title: Bolivia Joins ALBA Regional Bloc; Aligns with Venezuela and Cuba
note: Bolivia joined ALBA 2006 confirmed; Venezuelan oil and Cuban doctors program confirmed.

title: Eastern 'Media Luna' Departments Launch Autonomy Movement
note: Santa Cruz, Beni, Pando, Tarija autonomy movement confirmed; opposition to Morales government confirmed.

title: Pando Massacre Kills Pro-Government Indigenous Protesters
note: September 11, 2008 confirmed; final death toll ~13 (event states 'at least 13'); UNASUR summit response confirmed.

title: New Plurinational Constitution Approved by 61% of Voters
note: January 25, 2009 referendum; 61.43% approval confirmed.

title: Gasolinazo: Fuel Subsidy Removal Reversed After Mass Protests
note: December 2010 fuel price hike 70-80% and rapid reversal confirmed.

title: TIPNIS March Pits Indigenous Land Rights Against Development Road
note: 2011 march from Trinidad to La Paz against TIPNIS road confirmed; Morales suspended project confirmed.

title: Bolivia's Presidential Plane Forced Down Over Snowden Affair
note: July 2013 Vienna landing confirmed; France, Spain, Italy airspace denials confirmed. Event says Portugal also denied — Portugal was not listed in main sources as denying, minor discrepancy.

title: Referendum Rejects Morales's Bid for Fourth Presidential Term
note: 51.3% No confirmed; February 2016 confirmed; Constitutional Tribunal later cleared Morales to run confirmed.

title: Lake Poopo Dries Up in Climate-Driven Ecological Collapse
note: Dried up late 2015/early 2016 confirmed; Uru-Murato displacement confirmed; El Niño + climate change + water diversion confirmed.

title: ICJ Rules Bolivia Has No Right to Oblige Chile to Negotiate Sea Access
note: October 1, 2018; 12 votes to 3 against Bolivia confirmed.

title: Disputed Election Results and Political Crisis Force Morales to Resign
note: October 2019 election, OAS fraud report, police mutiny, military suggestion to resign, Morales left November 10 for Mexico confirmed.

title: Post-Crisis Massacres at Sacaba and Senkata Kill 23
note: Sacaba (9 dead, Nov 15) and Senkata (8 dead, Nov 19) confirmed. Total ~17–18 in those two incidents; event states 23 total for both — slightly elevated but within range of broader crisis death counts.

title: Luis Arce Wins Election, MAS Returns to Power
note: 55% result confirmed; October 2020 confirmed; repudiation of Anez government framing consistent with sources.

title: MAS Internal Split: Morales vs. Arce Fractures Bolivian Left
note: Arce-Morales public split and Evista/Arcista factionalism confirmed from 2021 onward.

title: Santa Cruz 36-Day Strike Paralyzes City Over Census Date
note: 36-day strike October 2022 confirmed; census dispute confirmed; government agreed to 2024 census confirmed.

title: General Zuniga Leads Failed Armored Coup Attempt
note: June 26, 2024 confirmed; armored vehicle ramming palace gate confirmed; ~3 hours confirmed; Zuniga arrested same day confirmed.

title: Severe Economic Crisis: Dollar and Fuel Shortages Deepen
note: 2024 fuel/dollar shortages and declining reserves confirmed by Cornell Business analysis.
